44_interl5441: In baptism, as in a bath, that he may receive back the moisture he had lost by denying. Hence Peter says to the parched Jews: “Repent, and be baptized every one of you, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.”
44_marg2980: Above, when the Ninevites repented and were saved, the prophet, asked the same, answered nothing, but approved God’s question by his silence; for, knowing God to be merciful and forgiving of evils, he did not grieve at the salvation of the Gentiles. But here, because the gourd has dried up and Israel withers, and he is asked pointedly, “Doest thou well to be angry for the gourd?”, he says boldly: “I do well to be sorrowful, even unto death; for I did not wish to save others in such a way that others perished, nor to win strangers in such a way that I lost my own.” So Christ mourns for Jerusalem even unto death, not his own death but the Jews’, that they may die denying and rise confessing the Son of God.
44_marg2981: As regards the people of the Gentiles. Hence Israel says plainly: “Lo, these many years do I serve thee, and thou never gavest me a kid; but for this thy son, which hath devoured thy living with harlots, thou hast killed the fatted calf.” He is not refuted in this, but hears: “All that I have is thine.” Yet it was meet to make merry for the brother’s return. For it was for the Gentiles that Christ’s precious blood was shed, and he went down to hell that that people might go up to heaven. No such toil was spent for the sons of Israel; and so he envies the younger brother.

44_marg2982: This can be understood of the age of infants, which is innocent and simple; and since the number of little ones is so great, it is plain that the multitude of older age was great. Or, since Nineveh is a great city, and in a great house there are vessels not only of gold but also of earthenware, it can be said that there was a great multitude which, before it did penance, did not know the difference between good and evil.
